| KS-SMS-T1 | 2026-10-14 | SMS tables: 24.011 j00 CP types (CP-DATA 01, CP-ACK 04, CP-ERROR 10) and RP MTIs 0-6 by direction; 23.038 j00 GSM 7-bit default alphabet (128 codes) and extension table (11). The Greek letters are Word SYMBOL fields, decoded through the Symbol font. Against pycrate: default table identical; extension identical in its 10 characters; pycrate also keeps 0x0D (CR2, 'NOTE 2: Void' in j00) and maps the reserved escape 0x1B to U+000E | spec/nas/23038/gsm7_alphabet.tsv, spec/nas/24011/*.tsv, M7 |
| KS-SMS-T2 | 2026-10-14 | M11 SMS check: CP, RP and TPDU each round-trip; every element pycrate (TS24011_PPSMS, TS23040_SMS) reads holds what ours read; tshark reads CP as gsm_a_dtap and RP as gsm_a_rp, and a TPDU inside an RP-DATA or RP-ACK built for its direction, because its dissector takes the direction from the RP layer (TS 23.040 9.2.3.1). 29 checks, all PASS | build/oracle/l3roundtrip.tsv, tests/oracles/ksimoracle/nasrt.py, M11 |
| KS-SMS-B1 | 2026-10-14 | TPDU decoding takes the direction, since TP-MTI alone does not name the type (TS 23.040 9.2.3.1), and for a report whether the carrying RP message is an RP-ERROR (TP-FCS present, 9.2.2.1a, 9.2.2.2a). TP-PI follows 9.2.3.27: a further TP-PI octet while bit 8 is set; a reserved bit set announces octets after TP-UD, which are kept as discarded rather than rejected; TP-UDL without TP-DCS means the default alphabet. GSM 7-bit packing follows TS 23.038 6.1.2.1, with fill bits after a user data header; a character outside the default alphabet and its extension table is an error, not a substitution | src/codec/nas/sms.hpp, tests/unit/nas/sms_test.cpp, M11 |
